title: IB/RDMA fallback characterization for multi-GPU inference
content:
Summary:
This is an empirical notebook capturing an investigation into observed inference tail-latency spikes that correlate with intermittent RDMA/IB path failures. We reproduced a fallback to TCP-based collectives and measured the impact on multi-GPU LLM-serving workloads (mixed tensor/pipeline parallel). Goals: quantify the perf delta between RDMA (IB/UCX path) and TCP fallback, find the triggers for fallback, and recommend mitigations for production deployments.

Motivation / why this matters:
- In our Dedicated clusters some pods intermittently fall back from IB/UCX to TCP when switch or driver conditions are suboptimal.
- For small-request, low-latency inference the collective path matters: even occasional fallbacks cause high tail latencies (p95/p99) and SLA violations.
- Need concrete numbers and reproducible troubleshooting steps to improve runtime heuristics and ops runbooks.

Hypotheses tested (short):
1) RDMA (RC/UD via Mellanox) yields significantly lower allreduce/allgather latency and higher bandwidth for the working set sizes common to KV-cache and activation exchange than TCP-over-Ethernet.
2) A mixture of switch QoS, MTU mismatch, and driver/firmware mismatches cause UCX/RDMA to fail and NCCL to fall back to TCP.
3) Fallback frequency increases proportionally with small-packet synchronous collectives (i.e., pipeline sync points).

Hardware + software baseline:
- Nodes: 2x DGX-style servers, each with 8x A100 40GB (NVLink-connected within node), dual-port Mellanox HDR200 NICs (ConnectX-7).
- Interconnect fabrics: Infiniband non-blocking leaf-spine fabric + 25/100Gb Ethernet mgmt network.
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 5.15 (stock for cluster).
- Drivers/stack: MLNX_OFED 5.8, UCX 1.14, NCCL 2.16, MXM disabled in experiments.
- Workload: a micro-bench harness simulating 2-stage pipeline + 2-way tensor sharding for a 13B model; also synthetic nccl-tests for controlled collectives.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Fabric modes: RDMA enabled (normal), RDMA intentionally disabled (module unbind or IB down), and pathological RDMA (MTU mismatch / QoS red drop).
- Collective types: allreduce (float32 activations), allgather (KV-cache keys), broadcast (weights).
- Message sizes: 64B, 512B, 4KB, 64KB, 1MB, 16MB.
- Concurrency: 1 inference request vs 8 concurrent requests per node (to stress interconnect).
- Repeats: 30 runs per cell, capture p50/p95/p99 and stddev.

Commands & reproducible steps (short):
- Bring up 2-node test cluster, make sure NCCL and UCX/IB are configured: export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO; export UCX_NET_DEVICES=mlx5_0:1; export NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0
- To force TCP fallback: sudo ifdown ib0 or echo 1 > /sys/module/mlx5_core/parameters/enable_hca (or set UCX_NET_DEVICES to lo).
- nccl-tests: build: git checkout nccl-tests; make MPI=0 CUDA=1; run: ./build/allreduce_perf -b 8 -e 16777216 -f 2 -g 8
- Serving harness: run inference harness with --tensor-parallel=2 --pipeline-stages=2 and a pinned seed to keep request sizes stable. Capture per-request timing via perftrace.

Key numeric findings (representative):
- Allreduce (8 GPUs across 2 nodes): 1MB message: RDMA median = 0.82 ms, p99 = 1.6 ms. TCP fallback median = 3.6 ms, p99 = 8.9 ms. (4.4x p99 increase)
- Allgather (small per-GPU KV shards ~512B per shard): RDMA median = 120 us, p99 = 460 us. TCP fallback median = 410 us, p99 = 1.2 ms. (3x tail)
- 16MB transfers (large model weight syncs): RDMA sustained bw ~30 GB/s aggregate, TCP fallback ~7 GB/s. (4.3x throughput drop)
- End-to-end inference tail impact: single-request p99 latency with mixed TP/PP RDMA = 42 ms; when a single collective falls back to TCP during the same request the p99 spikes to 135 ms. For 8 concurrent requests, p99 during intermittent fallback observed >450 ms and several timeouts in the harness.
- Variability: TCP fallback runs exhibited larger stddev and non-Gaussian long tails; some runs show repeated stalling (stall >100 ms) during KV-cache replays.

Root-cause signals observed:
- When fallback occurs, UCX logs show "no active rdma device" or connection retries; dmesg sometimes includes mlx5 WQ warnings after heavy microbursts.
- Switch counters: sporadic pause frames and ECN marking on the RDMA VLAN when microbursts coincide with background batch-migration traffic (ops job).
- MTU mismatch: a subset of hosts left at 1500 because of a provisioning script; others at 4096. When those hosts participated, UCX fallback rate increased.
- Firmware mismatch: older NIC firmware showed higher WQ errors under synthetic loads.

Interpretation / notes:
- For our critical small-message syncs (KV and activation exchange) RDMA is not just a constant speed boost — it meaningfully tightens the tail. Occasional fallback is catastrophic because an otherwise low-latency request path suddenly incurs a multi-ms stall.
- The fallback is not strictly deterministic: it is triggered by a combination of runtime retry thresholds (UCX), transient WQ/firmware errors, and network-level congestion signals.
- TCP fallback may be more resilient for sustained heavy throughput, but its latency distribution is too wide for low-latency inference.

Mitigations tested / short outcomes:
1) Strict configuration validation (preflight): check NIC firmware versions, MTU uniformity, and switch QoS shapes. When all hosts were standardized to MTU 4096 + firmware synced, fallback incidents dropped from ~1/200 runs to <1/2000.
2) UCX tuning: set UCX_RNDV_THRESH to a higher threshold to reduce rendezvous chatter for tiny messages; increased UCX_TLS to "rc,sm" only (avoid tcp if rc present) — reduced p99 by ~20% in some cases.
3) NCCL env tweaks: force NCCL to prefer IB: NCCL_IB_HCA=mlx5_0 NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=ib0; however this only prevents fallback if RDMA path is functional; it can cause failures if mistaken.
4) Runtime heuristics: implement early-detect probe in serving runtime (small UCX test on startup) and if unstable, gracefully degrade model parallelism (e.g., switch to local-replica fallback or increase async overlap) to avoid synchronous collectives. Proof-of-concept reduced p99 spikes in 60% of injected-failure runs.
5) Ops: do not colocate background bandwidth-heavy jobs on the same IB fabric as latency-sensitive inference. VLAN / QoS separation eliminated many ECN/pause-induced fallbacks.

Recommendations for product & infra:
- Add a cluster preflight that validates MTU, firmware, and UCX reachability. Fail fast on misconfigurations. (JIRA-PI-521)
- Expose a runtime flag to choose stricter collective fallback policies (conservative vs permissive) and document the production implications.
- Default console alerts: if UCX logs show repeated RDMA retries or NIC WQ errors, automatically create an incident with diagnostics bundle.
- Ops: deploy a small periodic UCX health-check pod on Dedicated clusters that triggers a canary allreduce and reports p50/p99.
- Longer term: experiment with partial redundancy for critical collective steps (e.g., dual-path sends or optimistic async replica stepping) to hide brief network pathology.

Action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Create infra preflight playbook and automated check (owner: Maya) — ticket created.
- [ ] Add runtime probe & safe-degrade code (owner: Lina) — prototype branch: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/892.
- [ ] Coordinate with infra to standardize MTU and schedule firmware rollouts (owner: Ops).
- [ ] Expand tests to >4 nodes and heterogeneous pod mixes (priority: medium).

Logs and artifacts (where to look):
- UCX logs: /var/log/ucx/ (gzipped traces attached to JIRA-PI-521).
- nccl-tests outputs: artifacts/nccl_allreduce_2024-10-19.tar.gz (linked in PR).
- perf traces: traces/p99_spike_2024-10-21.rec (samples of stack + timing).

Open questions / research ideas:
- Can we opportunistically route small collectives over NVLink intra-node and replicate head/kvs over RDMA while using TCP for bulk weight-syncs? (hybrid path optimization).
- Would enabling selective compression for small KV shards (very light-weight 2:1) reduce sensitivity to fallbacks? Cost/quality trade-offs unknown.
- Should Dedicated customers get a configuration SLA that enforces IB-only fabrics with onboarding checks?

Appendix: quick reproducer steps (minimal)
1) Run nccl microbench for controlled allreduce latency comparison: ./allreduce_perf -b 1 -e 1048576 -f 2 -g 8 -w 1 -c 30 > /tmp/allreduce.out
2) Force RDMA down on node-b: sudo ifdown ib0 (or unbind via "echo 0000:03:00.0 > /sys/bus/pci/drivers/mlx5_core/unbind") and rerun the same test. Compare p99 from /tmp/allreduce.out.
3) Run serving harness with envs: export NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0; export UCX_NET_DEVICES=mlx5_0:1; start harness and tail the per-request timings. Repeat with NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 to emulate TCP-only.

Notes for SRE playbook entry:
- Symptom: sudden increase in p99 for inference without CPU or GPU saturation. Check UCX/NCCL logs for fallback messages.
- Mitigation: temporarily shift live traffic to local-replica pool or reduce model parallelism to limit cross-node collectives until a maintenance window.

Concluding remark:
RDMA vs TCP fallback is not just a throughput delta — it is a tail-latency correctness problem for low-latency inference. Operational controls (configuration hygiene, health probes) combined with runtime-safe-degrade strategies will materially improve customer SLAs.
